column1: # sub-projects.tsv — the workable-item identifier roster (§11.4.54 / §11.4.148 D1).
# WHAT THIS FILE IS
# §11.4.148 makes the ticket-id PREFIX a consumer-supplied value, verbatim:
#   "the consuming project supplies its concrete DB path, id prefix,
#    external-tracker service + list/board id + field map + default-assignee
#    env var, and docs_chain context per §11.4.35."
# This file IS that supply. One row per identifier-bearing sub-project.
# THE FLEET IS DERIVED, THE NAMES ARE NOT.
# The SET of sub-projects is derived at run time from `.gitmodules` plus
# `helix-deps.yaml` — never from this file. This file supplies only the
# three-letter NAME for each derived member, because a name is an operator
# decision and cannot be measured. `workable-items roster` cross-checks the two:
# a submodule declared in `.gitmodules` with no row here is rc 2 (COULD NOT
# DETERMINE — never a pass), and a row here naming no declared submodule is a
# finding. A new submodule therefore cannot be silently dropped from tracking.
# RATIFICATION. `ratified` is `operator` only for the five identifiers the
# operator stated directly (2026-09-08: "Parent identifier: VSC, Identifiers for
# sub-projects: Workshop - WSP, ai_interviewing - AII, milosvasic.ru - MVR,
# vasic.digital - VDT, and for all others to be defined in same manner!").
# Every other row is `proposed` and is NOT approved — it is this agent's
# proposal awaiting operator ratification. `workable-items roster` prints the
# split so a proposal is never mistaken for a decision (§11.4.6).
# FORMAT — TAB-separated, mirroring scripts/check-registry.tsv's convention.
#   prefix   path                        class              ratified   note
# `class` closed set:
#   parent            the umbrella repository itself (not a submodule)
#   owned             an owned consumer of the governance cascade
#   governance-source the constitution submodule — the head of the cascade
#   third-party       not ours; no workable items are filed against it
